newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds and the rand drifted to a quiet close after an uneventful day in which markets consolidated recent gains.
"It's been pretty steady today. We've seen yields come down quite a lot in recent days, so you can expect some consolidation," said Neels Heyneke, bond trader at SMK Securities.
Both markets retraced after sharp after hours gains on Wednesday to trade in a tight range for most the day.

News that the money market shortage jumped back to 10.131 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.765 billion rand on Tuesday put a slight dampener on sentiment. But short-term rates were unaffected, with NCD rates actually nudging down fractionally, and bond dealers said players were focusing instead on this week's influx of foreign demand.
Bond Exchange figures showed non-residents bought a net 635 million rand of South African bonds in the first three days of the week.

Traders in both markets said underlying sentiment remained bullish, helped by a perception that the rand was stabilising and a continuing flow of Eurorand issues as investors roll over maturing bonds rather than taking the losses caused by the rand's 1996 fall.
"It's been an uneventful day -- really not a lot to report," said one senior forex trader.
"I still remain remain reasonably bullish for the rand. The longer it is in a stable range, the more attraction it offers for people who are looking to pick up the yield play."
Friday will see the release of April-December exchequer returns, which are expected to show the government on track to meet its target of a deficit equal to 5.1 percent of GDP in 1996/97.
The rand finished at 4.6555/6605 from a best 4.6400/6450 hit after hours on Wednesday and 4.6550/6600 seen at the local 1400 GMT close.
Against the crosses it was trading at 7.8041/8171 on sterling from 7.7781/7912 while on the mark it was at 0.3420/3425 from 0.3425/3429.
Leading banks edged down their three-month NCD rates to 17.25-17.50 percent from 17.30-17.50 while 90-day BA rates were unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent.
At the long end of the market the R150 bond stood at 15.62, unchanged from 1400 GMT on Wednesday, after trading down to 15.55 percent after hours.

Foreigners bought a net 268.44 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 286.21 million rands on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said. Nominal cumulative turnover was 8.68 billion rand from 7.11 billion.
